points.what: LATAM orders fell 9.0% WoW, contributing -11 to the week's order change, the largest regional drag.
points.so_what: LATAM was the biggest driver behind orders finishing below the weekly target.

points.what: North America orders rose 7.4% WoW, contributing +14, the largest positive contribution among regions.
points.so_what: North America growth partly offset declines elsewhere but was not enough to lift total orders to target.

points.what: Facebook orders fell 18.6% WoW, contributing -11 to the week's change, the largest negative contribution among traffic sources.
points.so_what: The order decline was concentrated in a smaller channel, while the dominant Search channel continued to grow.

points.what: AOV was $82.94, down 0.1% WoW and down 2.0% YoY.
points.so_what: Orders grew 51.4% YoY while AOV fell, so revenue growth is coming from more orders, not bigger baskets.

points.what: Cancellation rate was 14.2%, up 0.6pp WoW and up 2.1pp YoY.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations represents about $706 in revenue, so this week's rise works against revenue attainment.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 16 Mar was 9.3%, down 0.2pp WoW and flat YoY.
points.so_what: A stable-to-improving return rate is not adding the same pressure to revenue that rising cancellations and falling AOV currently are.

points.what: New signups rose 9.7% WoW to 259, while orders fell 0.5% WoW.
points.so_what: Customer growth continued even as order volume slipped, so the order dip is isolated from new customer acquisition.

summary.headline: Mixed week: orders were 95.0% of target while revenue was 100.4% of target, and YTD revenue remains behind target at 93.0%.

points.what: Orders were 851, 95.0% of target, down 0.5% WoW.
points.so_what: Orders missed the weekly target even though revenue beat it, so the shortfall sits in volume, not order value.

points.what: Revenue was 60547, 100.4% of target, though down 1.3% WoW.
points.so_what: Revenue cleared the weekly target, but YTD revenue is still only 93.0% of target, so one ahead week does not close the year gap.

points.what: New signups were 259, up 9.7% WoW and 10.2% YoY.
points.so_what: Signup growth topped order growth this week, so the order dip did not come from fewer new customers arriving.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 14.2%, up 0.6pp WoW and up 2.1pp YoY.
points.so_what: A cancellation rate rising on both bases works against the week's revenue target attainment.

points.what: Orders were 95.0% of target with a gap of -45, while revenue was 100.4% of target with a gap of 249, for the week.
points.so_what: Orders behind target while revenue is ahead makes this a mixed week against target, not a clean beat or miss.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 100.4%, ahead of target, with 823539 still required to reach the full quarter target over the next 12 weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter is off to an ahead-of-target start, but a large amount remains to reach the full-quarter target.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 93.0%, behind target, with a required weekly run-rate of 79813 versus a current 8-week run-rate of 57975.
points.so_what: At this pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach.

points.what: Cancellation rate was 14.2%, up 0.6pp WoW and up 2.1pp YoY.
points.so_what: Rising cancellations on both bases is a bad-direction move that erodes revenue even when orders hold up.

points.what: AOV was $82.94, down 0.1% WoW and down 2.0% YoY.
points.so_what: A shrinking AOV on both bases means basket value is not keeping pace with order growth, a drag on revenue.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is 57975 against a required weekly run-rate of 79813 for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: At the current pace the full-year revenue target is out of reach without a step-up from recent weeks.
